title: Regulated Deployments — Evidence Binder & Seller Playbook
content:
Purpose: create a compact, field-usable evidence bundle and objection-response playbook that sellers and solutions engineers can use when running regulated pilots (VPC / on-prem / air-gapped) where security, auditability and control-plane language matters. This is a living pilot artifact intended for quick customization per prospect.

Audience and use cases:
- Primary: AE + Solutions Engineer during discovery, procurement and pilot kickoff.
- Secondary: CISO/security reviewer, procurement, cloud/infra ops team, internal legal for data residency checks.
- Use cases: 1) accelerating security gating for pilots; 2) reducing back-and-forth during SOC/ISO/PCI evidence requests; 3) framing control-plane responsibilities and fallback guarantees.

Three core positioning pillars (short):
1) Clear responsibility split — We provide a lightweight private control plane that you can host in your VPC or on-prem. Your data path and compute remain under your network controls; our control plane operates via defined management endpoints and optional delegated admin tokens.
2) Evidence-first — We bundle the artifacts that auditors ask for early: network diagrams, attacker-surface mapping, crypto/KMS design notes, deployment checklist, and a reproducible demo for verification.
3) Operational fallbacks — Pilot SLA and rollback playbooks that prioritize availability and safety: automatic model pinning, canary rollback, and traffic quarantine.

Suggested quick structure for the evidence binder (single-page index + attachments):
- Cover note: one-sentence summary of what the binder includes and who to contact inside Redwood.
- Architecture diagram: network flow (customer VPC, private control plane, optional proxy), ports, authentication flows.
- Responsibility matrix: who does what (Redwood vs customer) for credentials, KMS, backups, logs, artifact retention.
- Audit artifacts: table of available artifacts (SOC-like checklist): configuration snapshots, TLS cert fingerprints, KMS key policy excerpts, container image SBOMs, SRE runbooks.
- Pilot runbook: steps we will execute during the two-week pilot, tests to validate (end-to-end request path, data exfiltration test, simulated outage).
- Compliance snippet pack: canned answers for common questions (data residency, retention, deletion, encryption at rest/in transit, key ownership).
- Demo checklist: reproducible steps the customer security team can run in <60 minutes to validate claims.

Top seller objection threads and recommended responses (concise):
- Objection: "Control plane is managed — we can’t allow external management."
  Response: "We support two deployment choices for the control plane: customer-hosted control plane image or customer-managed control plane service in your VPC. When you choose customer-hosted, we hand over the deployment artifacts and we only provide a signed operator for updates; no secret keys leave your environment."

- Objection: "How do we know you can’t access our data?"
  Response: "Request flow summary: inference tokens and model weights never transit Redwood-managed public endpoints for private deployments. We provide network-level policies (SGs, ACLs) and a read-only audit stream you can verify. We also run an independent verification demo during pilot where the customer observes traffic flows live."

- Objection: "We need encryption keys under our control (HSM/KMS)."
  Response: "Supported: external KMS integration (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure KeyVault, or on-prem HSM). Our control plane can be configured to never store plaintext keys and to use customer-side signing for critical operations. We include a KMS policy template as part of the binder."

- Objection: "What happens if Redwood endpoint is unreachable?"
  Response: "Design for graceful degradation: runtime can operate with pinned models and local KV cache; critical inference paths can be routed to local-only mode. For control-plane unavailability we provide documented fallback and emergency access flows so your ops team can continue serving."

Competitor framing and counter-claims (short bullet points):
- Managed cloud provider endpoints (competitor claim: "we are simpler") — Counter: Simplicity comes with opaque telemetry and shared control plane. Emphasize auditability and ability to host the control plane inside customer network.
- Self-hosted open-source runtimes (competitor claim: "cheaper and fully under your control") — Counter: Total control is possible, but the customer pays for operational maturity. We provide hardened images, SRE-runbooks, and an SLA-backed pilot with knowledge transfer to reduce time-to-production risk.
- Incumbent enterprise vendors (competitor claim: "we’re compliant by default") — Counter: Ask which specific evidence they will hand over for pilot auditors. Our binder makes evidence explicit and reproducible.

Minimum evidence pack (what to attach to an initial seller intro email):
1) Network diagram PDF (annotated).
2) Responsibility matrix CSV.
3) KMS policy template (txt).
4) Pilot runbook (md).
5) Demo checklist (md).
6) One-page control-plane threat model (pdf).

Pilot engagement template (recommended two-week structure):
- Week 0 (pre-kickoff): exchange IP allowlists, service account keys, and expected time windows.
- Week 1: deploy private control plane (customer-hosted or VPC-managed), smoke tests, run demo checklist with customer security team.
- Week 2: run adversarial verification tests, operational handover, collect feedback and a short ATO-style note for procurement.

Fast email snippet for initial outreach (to CISO/security):
Subject: Evidence pack for short regulated pilot — [Company name] & Redwood
Body (one paragraph): "We know security reviews slow pilots. Attached is a compact evidence binder we use in regulated pilots: network diagram, KMS policy template, pilot runbook and a reproducible demo the security team can run in under an hour. If you’re open, we can align on a two-week pilot that leaves control and keys in your environment and provides artifacts for your auditors. — Asha (solutions lead)"

SRE/SE quick-reference checklist (for internal use during calls):
- Confirm deployment mode (customer-hosted control plane vs Redwood-managed VPC tenant).
- Confirm KMS choice and whether keys are customer-owned.
- Confirm IP allowlist and whether there is a proxy requirement.
- Share evidence binder link and highlight demo checklist.
- Agree pilot rollback/termination trigger points and documentation owner.

Open questions to add to binder (follow up with product/infra):
- Formalize the language for "delegated admin token" lifecycle and rotation cadence.
- Standardize the minimum telemetry we will expose to customers in private deployments.
- Create a one-page ATO-style summary for US federal buyers (FISMA/DoD speak).

Next steps (owner: Asha):
- Convert this draft into a one-click zip template with named files (Due: 2026-03-20).
- Run two internal dry-run demos and collect timings (Due: 2026-03-27).
- Hand off to AE enablement for a short playbook with role-based talking points (Due: 2026-04-05).

Notes / voice of the field (raw snippets collected from SEs):
- "They want to see a real KMS key policy not just a promise."
- "Show me rollback steps up front — procurement tracks that as technical debt."
- "Auditors get bored quickly — give them a 45 minute reproducible demo they can tick off."

End of doc.
